Wiley Post. The pioneering aviator of the nineteen-thirties who set multiple speed and distance records through sheer daring. In nineteen thirty-one, Post circumnavigated the world in eight days and sixteen hours, the fastest around-the-world flight at that time. Throughout the decade, he set multiple transcontinental speed records, including a nineteen thirty-four flight from Los Angeles to New York in under seven hours. Post designed the first practical pressure cabin to enable high-altitude flight, innovations that extended altitude records and influenced aircraft design for decades. He flew the Lockheed Vega, a fast monoplane that became his signature aircraft for record attempts. A patch over one eye, from an earlier accident, became his distinctive feature throughout his career but did not slow his achievements. In nineteen thirty-five, Post died in a plane crash near Point Barrow, Alaska, with humorist Will Rogers aboard. His rapid progression from postal pilot to record-setter exemplified the daring spirit of aviation's golden age. Post shared his era with fellow record-setters Howard Hughes and Charles Lindbergh, and with Amelia Earhart, who was also exploring distance and endurance records.
